about: The finished cuts Krish named as the production quality floor for video, for briefs and the Critic. The bar itself, quality by quality, is docs/production/THE_BAR.md; this file names the files exactly, says what is and is not established about each one's identity, lists the reference moments and each quality's comparison points by timestamp, and carries the quality names. The page and this file must agree on all three (python3 scripts/floor.py --check). scripts/floor.py prints the bar whole for the makers in full_bar_for_makers and a one-line pointer for the other makers in applies_to_makers, before the rejection standards. Only Krish adds a reference, changes the bar or moves its standing from draft to approved.

ruling.words: the video production quality standards for the latest Friday (AI Passports) and Monday (character.ai) pieces are the floor for what I expect in terms of premium quality, motion design, cinematic feeling, movement, branding etc. Friday's is a voiceover format and Monday's a regular split screen format. Do not be intensely literal here as every piece is different, but I want you to get a feel for the standards we are never to fall beneath ever again
ruling.correction: the long voiceover video is still being post produced so dont just assume that the voiceover format only has a 90sec version, you are only to look for production quality standards

standing_note: The qualities below are the engine's reading of the cuts he named; he has not approved their wording. Follow them; only he approves them.
principle: Every frame looks designed and owned by the brand. Motion carries the argument instead of decorating it. The world has light, focus, depth and material. The brand works as a system. Proof is real, dated and designed. The sound is finished. Put each new moment beside the named reference moment, in motion, at full size, with sound, and ask: would it sit beside that without looking cheaper, flatter, slower, busier or less owned? Do not copy the references: each piece finds its own object, its own devices and its own big moment, and reaches the same craft with them.
measured_values: Context about the references, never targets. Lengths, shapes, cut counts, frame timings, levels, tempo and sampled colours describe these three files only. They are kept out of config/reference-cuts.json on purpose, and floor.py --check refuses a measured field written there (duration, aspect, bpm, lufs and the like); it cannot see a figure inside a sentence, so none is written in one either. The existing gates set the only numeric limits.

related.production_contract: docs/MEDIA_STANDARD.md and config/media-standard.json (its exemplars are never production inputs either)
related.rejection_floor: config/rejection-floor.json, read through scripts/floor.py: what he rejected; this file is what he named as the floor to reach
related.ve_key_frames: config/ve/design-lock.json formats.*.keyframes: approved key frames for one ve format and module, matched by structural similarity; the reference cuts are never matched pixel for pixel
related.style_bank: config/style-references.json: every style in the bank has to reach this bar
related.brand: docs/STUDIO.md (makeyourmindup branding) and config/ve/brand-tokens.json own the palette, type and brand rules
related.logos: docs/MEDIA_STANDARD.md, Design before labels: outside brands appear as their accurate official marks, never invented or redrawn (and draft floor standard s53328195a4); nothing in the bar loosens that

qualities.name: Premium finish: every frame looks made and owned
Motion that explains: one visual idea carries the argument
Motion craft: weight, ease, stagger, exits
Cinematic feel: light, focus, depth, a living world
Movement and pace: alive, and timed to meaning
Typography: few voices, fixed jobs, words that add
Composition and layout: the whole frame, one focal point
Colour and grade: an owned palette where colour means something
Texture and depth: material, never a flat template
Transitions: motivated, seamless, one loud moment at most
Captions: burned in, branded, calm, in sync
Proof visuals: real, dated and designed
Krish on camera: real, steady, in sync

reference_moments.what: USING A / CHINESE AI? builds on a living phone plate, with headline, coral slab, italic deck, word-by-word caption and a card tracked into the screen. The opening statement and the type system.
The CHESKY TO BLOOMBERG quote card tracked into the phone while the plate sways, with a hand-drawn underline and server racks soft behind. Cinematic plate and named source.
A dark brand beat; TWO PASSPORTS lands first, then the page rises and fades up. A chapter transition.
The CHINA stamp slams in oversized and tilted, then settles. Motion with weight.
A mint marker loop drawn round CHINA in a few frames. Hand-drawn emphasis on the one thing that matters.
Passport paper with grain, security lines, halftone round the flag and stickers with offset shadows. Texture.
'? OUT OF 3' held back, then filled to 2. A number withheld until it is proved.
Headline, a phone card with a circled entry, a caption and a mint band, all four readable. Composition.
The phone swings and pushes into the dated DeepSeek screen recording, with the sentence underlined and quoted. The signature move, spent on the proof.
The OUR CALL card held to be read while the captions step aside. A read-hold and caption discipline.
The caption slab becomes the brand band strapped across the passport. A branded close that completes the metaphor.
The opening card builds piece by piece in reading order. Staggered build.
MILLIONS MADE FRIENDS HERE arrives word by word as spoken while the grid spreads. Type in time with speech.
The BANKRUPT impact (flash, oversized slam, crawling tapes, debris) while the grid loses its colour. The one loud moment, with colour telling the story.
A torn-edged receipt rises, its lines build, and its mint figure matches the caption's mint chip. Texture, proof and captions speaking one language.
An article blurred except for the quoted phrase. Focus used as a lens, and honest proof.
THE PEOPLE rides an arrow into Disney's slot while THE LAWSUITS stays behind. Motion that explains.
Empty slots fill as each company is named, then the counter slows hard into 75%. State change on the word.
One end card, its lines revealed one at a time, the underline drawing on. One close.
Measured, not yet heard: the sting under the cold open, a low bed under the hook and a tight voice edit. Sound finish.
A stage with a grid, two drifting light pools and a vignette. A lit ground.
Logos drop into the RENTED box, then the VOID stamp lands. Transitions that carry the thought on.
A slow push on the CTO document with one phrase in focus, then it defocuses as the receipt springs up and settles. Cinematic hold, transition and craft.
Comparison receipts count up into a side-by-side board. Proof that sums up.
The counter rolls to 75% on 'I'm 75% sure', with a small sound hit (the hit measured, not yet heard). Sync of picture, word and sound.
